issues.kind: NO OUTCOME / TWO READINGS (law 2 Carried way; law 2 (a)-(c))
issues.claim: S3 lays two wall lines besides the stage-1 boundary - a merged pair's cross wall at (6) and a castle's curtain at (8) - and neither gives a carried way standing before the stage a gate, a re-route or an exclusion where the line crosses its ground course. The laws: the meeting's raised way includes 'the way it carries' (l. 2584-2590), the cross wall and a castle's curtain are enclosing walls; law 2 Carried way (l. 2780-2793): 'A road deck's carried way meets every enclosing wall on its ground course by the gate law (§5.3's gate row), its gate where the wall crosses that course beyond the foot', else re-routed by law 2 (b) 'through the nearest gate of that wall', else law 2 (c); the fixed-place sentence (l. 3250): 'A castle sited after the raised way is sited clear of it, never reshaped'; §5.3's gate row (l. 9946): 'a way on ground part 0 crosses an enceinte's trace only at a gate'. The pipeline: S3 (6) (l. 6229-6232) lays the cross wall 'with a gate where the inter-nucleus route crosses it' and meets each standing raised way for its line and the inter-nucleus route's gate only, naming no carried way; S3 (7) (l. 6234) gives a carried way 'a gate of the stage where T = t_1 crosses its ground course' - the boundary only, while the cross wall lies on T's partition line; S3 (8)'s hard filter (l. 6250-6251) keeps only '(5) route[s]' off the claim and admits every claim 'law 1 admits', and law 1 has no clause on a curtain across a carried way's ground course, the castle having one town-side gate (§4.8 Gates, l. 8392); §4.1 (l. 5797-5798) makes a creation prefix's declared road a fixed route of S4 and S5b. Class (B)'s B2 row for R0 (adjudication-r7y.md l. 178) resolves only the cross wall's line and the inter-nucleus route's gate. Case: a twin-town or polycentric CITY merged at S3 (6) from a skeleton declaring a raised road inside the union whose ground course beyond its foot crosses the partition line (or a regeneration keeping such a locked road), and a castle whose best claim straddles such a carried way. Builder 1 builds the text: the cross wall (or curtain) laid across the ground course with no gate; §5.3's gate row fails; F-WALL's detection (l. 9862) 'an arterial or a carried way given no lawful gate and no re-route' runs the raised-way rung and leaves stage 1 unwalled, or, as 'a non-gate way reaches the trace', the non-raised ladder's last rung cuts the declared way. Builder 2 builds the laws as one resolver: a gate of the cross wall where it crosses the ground course beyond the foot, moved along the way by (a), else the way re-routed through the cross wall's gate (b), else the cross wall not laid (c, as S3 (6)'s own (c)); the castle sited clear of the way. Builder 1's outcomes are the two Part P pass 8 ruled against J144 and J147 (1) as the program reads them (PRB7H-GEN-04 (i), (ii)); no valid choice (J151). No bar runs it: T110-2 (2)'s declared-viaduct variant (l. 19356-19359) lays the cross wall beneath the deck, not across the ground course.

issues.claim: The moat-deck pick written for VF7x-GEN-06 re-routes 'the arterial or carried way' wherever it would meet its gate's channel more than 10° off the normal, and names no exception for a shape-locked carried way, which the laws never move. The laws: law 2 (b) (l. 2815-2823) may move 'a ground way not shape-locked (a wall's own way, a road deck's carried way)' and 'Never ... anything shape-locked (law 1 (9), (10))'; law 2 Carried way (l. 2790-2793): 'the carried way — a Tier-3 way, unless itself shape-locked — is re-routed'; law 1 (10) (l. 2739-2743): 'a thing held in ... shape its outline and size (held), changed by no op but one that names it', shape including 'a Tier-3 thing's local course (law 2 (b))' (l. 2664-2667); J147 (owner): 'a shape lock is honoured where a raised way meets a wall', the meeting including the wall's moat and the way the raised way carries (l. 2584-2590). The pipeline: S3 (10) (l. 6299) lays 'one deck ... at a carried way's gate (7)' where 'the carried way' crosses the channel, 'perpendicular to it'; §4.3 Routes (l. 6423-6426) re-solves the stretch of 'a carried way standing before the stage' 'through the gate's deck, which continues the gate passage straight across the moat, perpendicular to it'; S5a Outer moats (l. 6646-6648): 'the arterial or carried way is re-routed between the gate and its next pinned node beyond the channel where it would meet the channel more than 10° off its normal'. Case (from the milestone that carries the shape lock, J147, J150): a generation from a skeleton declaring a raised road whose ground way the user shape-locked, or a Regenerate (keep) / New random with that lock, the stage-1 boundary (or a stage-2 boundary with a wet outer moat) crossing the way's ground course beyond its foot, the way meeting the wet moat more than 10° off its normal. Builder 1 builds the pick as written and re-routes the shape-locked way through a perpendicular deck - a change of a shape-held thing by an op that does not name it (law 1 (10)), the move law 2 (b) bars. Builder 2 builds the laws: the way unmoved, its deck laid where the channel's banks cross it, oblique (VF7x-GEN-06's option (ii), which adjudication-r7y.md judged lawful and passing every bar). Builder 1's outcome breaks law 1 (10) and the owner's J147 as the program reads it: no valid choice (J151). §4.3's ±10° deck bar runs on B-CITY, which holds no carried way, so builder 2 fails no named test.

issues.claim: adjudication-r7y.md gave two wall lines their own law 2 (c) at generation - a merged pair's cross wall not laid (B2, S3 (6)) and a top-up's arc kept as it stood (B7, S5d) - but the three readers that list law 2 (c)'s generation outcomes carry them unevenly. §5.2 F-WALL's ladder (l. 9862) excepts 'a top-up's arc, which §4.4 S5d keeps as it stood' from the raised-way rung but not the cross wall, though F-WALL is S3's class (l. 5719) and its detection's 'a trace with no lawful crossing of a standing raised way' reads a cross wall too. §4.13's wall cell (l. 9719): 'a wall laid after it with no lawful shape taking law 2 (c) on its path — F-WALL's raised-way rung at generation and a regeneration, §5.2' - neither the cross wall nor the top-up arc. §5.4's W_RAISED_MEETING (l. 9992), 'each outcome of §2.7's laws, law 2 (c), at generation, a regeneration and a village derivation', lists the cross wall (D3) but not the top-up arc, which S5d reports only under F-BUDGET-STAGE (l. 6728). S3 (6) and S5d state their own (c), which decide each case; no bar counts W_RAISED_MEETING for a top-up. A reader omitting an outcome its rule names (VF7w-GEN-03's grade).

issues.claim: T110-2 (6)'s first clause (l. 19585-19588: '(1)'s c15 fixture ... with its aqueduct placement-locked, regenerated (keep): the routes, the ring, its strips, band, towers and gates byte-identical in the model digest (§6.2)') and row W3·C2 (l. 3348: 'so a ring re-derived on its old trace reproduces its strips, band, towers, gates and vaults') promise that a ring re-derived under a raised way the regeneration keeps reproduces the old trace, but the fixture does not fix that state, because the order of the meeting changes at the regeneration. At the first run the aqueduct is S6's, laid after the ring: the support step slid each station off the smoothed trace's band 'to the nearest clear position' (l. 2539-2549), so a support can stand at that band's edge. At the regeneration the kept aqueduct is older than every stage (law 2 Newer, l. 2764-2767), and S3 (9)'s pull searches only the shapes the laws admit, 'its line read with the band and wall strips it carries there' (l. 6609), before smoothing; law 1 (2) bars a standing support in the band of an over crossing (l. 2707-2709), as fixture (1)'s is. Where smoothing moved the line away from such a support, the old pulled line is not admitted and the pull returns another; and S5a Trace (3)'s guard (l. 6613-6615) can refuse a smoothing move the first run made. T110-2's lead (S0, l. 19265-19273) makes the bar assert the laws' outcome where its words and that outcome differ, so no correct build fails it: a clause naming a state its fixture may not hold.
